specialRules.name: Prey Instinct
specialRules.text:
The Rangda are hunters before they are anything else, and the more their quarry falters, the surer the kill.

When a Model with this Special Rule makes a Shooting Attack or a Melee Attack against a Target Unit that has one or more of the Pinned, Suppressed, Stunned or Routed Tactical Statuses, that attack gains the Critical Hit (X) Special Rule, where X is 7 minus the number of those Tactical Statuses the Target Unit has, to a minimum of 4: Critical Hit (6+) against a Unit with one, (5+) against a Unit with two, and (4+) against a Unit with three or more. If the weapon already has a Critical Hit (X) Special Rule, use whichever value is lower. Attacks that make no Hit Test, such as Template weapons, gain nothing.

specialRules.name: Horror of the Taken
specialRules.text:
Everyone who fought the Rangda saw it happen at least once: a squad that did not die but was carried off, and came back wearing collars.

When a Unit that includes any Models with this Special Rule destroys an enemy Unit in combat (the last Model of that Unit is Removed as a Casualty by its Melee Attacks), every other enemy Unit with any Model within 6" of the destroyed Unit's last Model must make a Leadership Check. Any Unit that fails gains the Routed Tactical Status.

specialRules.name: Neural Collars
specialRules.text:
Every thrall wears a collar that carries its masters' will into its nerves, so that it marches into fire without a sound.

While any Model in a Unit that only includes Models with this Special Rule is within 12" of a friendly Model with the Rangda Trait, that Unit automatically passes any Leadership Check or Cool Check it is required to make.

While no Model in the Unit is within 12" of a friendly Model with the Rangda Trait, the Leadership and Cool Characteristics of its Models become 5, and no Reactions may be declared for the Unit.

specialRules.name: Collar-master
specialRules.text:
A Rangdan officer can drive a collar past what the body wearing it can take.

Once per Player Turn, at the start of the Fight Sub-Phase, the Controlling Player of a Model with this Special Rule that is on the battlefield may select one friendly Unit with the Neural Collars Special Rule that has any Model within 12" of it. Until the end of that Phase, all Models in the selected Unit gain a modifier of +1 to their Strength and Attacks Characteristics. At the end of that Phase, the selected Unit suffers D3 wounds, allocated by its Controlling Player, against which no Saving Throws or Damage Mitigation Tests may be taken.

specialRules.name: Worm Gestalt
specialRules.text:
A Slaugth is thousands of sentient worms in a skin of mucus. Bolts and blades pass through a body that simply closes up behind them; fire is another matter.

Models with this Special Rule have the Feel No Pain (5+) Special Rule. This Damage Mitigation Test may not be taken against wounds inflicted by any Weapon with the Flame Trait or the Aflame (X) Special Rule.

specialRules.name: Carrion Feast
specialRules.text:
The Slaugth eat the dead as they fight, and the worms that make them up grow fat on it.

Each time a Model with this Special Rule Removes an enemy Model as a Casualty with a Melee Attack, it regains one lost Wound (or Hull Point). A Model cannot regain more Wounds or Hull Points than its starting value.

reactions.name: Living Shields
reactions.text:
The masters have never stood in front of their own herd. When the guns turn on them, the collars drag the thralls into the line of fire.

Trigger: The Reactive Player may declare a Living Shields Advanced Reaction at the start of Step 3 of the Shooting Attack sequence, when an enemy Unit targets a friendly Unit that only includes Models with the Rangda Trait and is not a Vehicle, and a friendly Unit with the Neural Collars Special Rule has any Model within 3" of the target.

Cost: 1 Reaction Point.

Effect: The Unit with the Neural Collars Special Rule becomes the target of the Shooting Attack instead, even if it would not normally be a legal target, as long as at least one of its Models is within range of at least one of the attacking Unit's Weapons. Weapons that cannot reach it may not make attacks. A Unit may only be selected for this Reaction once per Player Turn.

reactions.name: The Hunt Closes
reactions.text:
Prey that stumbles is prey that dies. A Rangdan hunt-pack moves the moment its quarry falters.

Trigger: The Reactive Player may declare The Hunt Closes Advanced Reaction when an enemy Unit with one or more Tactical Statuses ends a move in the Movement Phase within 12" of a friendly Unit that only includes Models with the Rangda Trait and the Infantry or Paragon Type.

Cost: 1 Reaction Point.

Effect: The Reacting Unit may move up to its Movement Characteristic. It must end that move closer to the Target Unit and may not end it within 1" of any enemy Model.

gambits.name: Hunter's Stare
gambits.text:
When selecting a Gambit, the Controlling Player of a Model with the Rangda Trait can select Hunter's Stare instead of any others available to that Model.

If this Gambit is selected, the opposing Model must make a Cool Check, applying any Fear (X) modifiers. If the Check is failed, the Controlling Player of the Model that selected Hunter's Stare gains a +2 modifier to the Focus Roll for this round of the Challenge.

gambits.name: Feast of Memories
gambits.text:
When selecting a Gambit, the Controlling Player of a Model with the Slaugth Trait can select Feast of Memories instead of any others available to that Model.

If this Gambit is selected and the opposing Model is Removed as a Casualty in this round of the Challenge, the Model that selected Feast of Memories regains all of its lost Wounds and gains one Special Rule of the opposing Model (chosen by its Controlling Player; not a Type, Sub-Type or Trait) for the rest of the battle. It has eaten the memory of how to fight that way.

traits.name: Xenos
traits.text: The 'Xenos' trait replaces the Allegiance Trait for Xenos factions. An army that includes models with the Xenos Trait may still include models with either the Loyalist or Traitor Trait, but not the other.

traits.name: Rangda
traits.text: The Rangda themselves: tall, lithe, vaguely vulpine hunters out of the Halo Stars. Rules that refer to Rangdan Models refer to Models with this Trait.

traits.name: Thrall
traits.text: Imperial soldiers taken from conquered worlds and fitted with neural collars. They keep their own wargear and fight their former allies with it. Models with this Trait also have the Xenos Trait: they fight for their masters now.

traits.name: Slaugth
traits.text: The carrion-worms that follow the Rangdan hunts. Slaugth Models are not Rangda: they do not count as friendly Rangdan Models for the Neural Collars Special Rule and do not have the Prey Instinct Special Rule.
